status: v0.4.0: ready for scale-up. Derived from 61 documents; revised over three pilot rounds (see data/policy/pilot-*/REPORT.md). Round 3 was a holdout: misfit rate 1.9%, independent agreement 96% (kind) and 92% (exact) on 4 documents.

states.none_exists: The document says outright that there is no such thing here. A positive finding; needs a quote.
states.not_stated: The document was read and does not answer the question. Not evidence that nothing exists.
states.not_applicable: The question does not apply to this document's audience or level, or a gate variable rules it out.

misfit: A document that DOES answer but has no honest value on the list is left value:null with a misfit_note. It is never forced to the nearest value. Misfits are the evidence for revising a vocabulary.

domains.assessed_work: Rules for students' assessed or submitted work (coursework, exams, theses as assessed work).
domains.teaching_practice: Rules for how staff teach, mark, give feedback or handle student material.
domains.research_conduct: Rules for doing, writing, publishing or reviewing research.
domains.funding_applications: Rules for preparing or assessing funding applications.
domains.administration: Rules for professional-services, administrative or operational use.
domains.public_services: Commitments about public-sector or citizen-facing use.

domainsRule: A document covers a domain if it contains at least one rule, commitment or recommendation about it, whoever it is addressed to. A student guide that says staff will not use AI to grade covers teaching_practice. Variables about what a person must do with AI in something they submit (use_*, disclosure_*) apply to every domain where someone submits work; only the assessment machinery (silent default, tiers, labelling) is tied to assessed_work.

rowRules.evidence_quotes: For multi variables, supply evidence_quotes: {value_id: quote} with a verbatim quote for EVERY value. One quote cannot evidence several values. evidence_quote remains for single-valued variables and misfits.
rowRules.audience_scope: Optional. When one document gives different rules to two audiences (UKRI: applicants vs assessors; a staff policy with a student box), code the variable once per audience with audience_scope set to the audience id. Default is the whole document. A variable's rows must be unique per (document, variable, audience_scope).
rowRules.general_permission_only: If a document states only a blanket permission ('as a rule AI use is permitted') and lists no per-use rules, leave the use_* variables not_stated and record the general stance in institutional_posture and default_when_silent. Do not infer per-use permissions from a general statement.
rowRules.rule_source: Optional (not the numeric `basis` column). Where a rule comes from: own_text (default), template_wording (sample wording the document offers others to adopt, e.g. Harvard's sample syllabus policies), or quoted_other_policy (another body's wording quoted inside this document, e.g. a University paragraph inside a school policy). Cells with basis other than own_text are analysed separately from the document's own rules.
